section_summary.extract_value: This section reports assessment of interoceptive awareness (IA) using the 32-item self-report Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness (MAIA) comprising eight subscales, with responses on a 6-point scale and subscale scores computed as item means (higher = greater IA). Internal consistency (ordinal coefficient) values are reported for each subscale (Noticing = .71; Attention regulation = .87; Emotional Awareness = .82; Self-Regulation = .86; Body Listening = .76; Trusting = .79; Not-Distracting = .53; Not-Worrying = .60), and the Not-Distracting and Not-Worrying subscales were excluded from further analyses due to poor reliability.
section_summary.evidence_source: We assessed IA using the Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness (MAIA; Mehling et al., 2012), a 32-item self-report measure that comprises eight subscales. Scores for each subscale were computed as the mean of all associated items, and higher scores reflect greater IA. Values for each subscale were as follows: Noticing = .71; Attention regulation = .87; Emotional Awareness = .82; Self-Regulation = .86; Body Listening = .76; Trusting = .79; Not-Distracting = .53; Not-Worrying = .60.Although the latter two values were consistent with previous research (Mehling, Acree, Stewart, Silas, & Jones, 2018; Mehling, 2016), they are indicative of poor internal inconsistency (Gadermann, Guhn, & Zumbo, 2012) and so were excluded from further analyses.
